reason: At step 5 the proof used lem-field-is-a-commutative-ring as [F1], whose Statement directly gives that the given field is an integral domain; step 1.1 then feeds that conclusion into cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-domain-is-a-domain. The planned route through def-field and def-zero-divisor-and-integral-domain was not taken because the stronger lemma supplies the combined result without re-unfolding both definitions. The replacement is published on order 46, earlier than this order-53.2 page.

At step 5 the Definition included the residue-field clause that R/m is a field. The added thm-quotient-is-field-iff-ideal-maximal is the exact result that turns maximality of the unique maximal ideal m into that field conclusion. It is published on order 48, earlier than this order-53.2 page.

At step 5 the universal-property proof had to establish its domain and identify its codomain concretely. def-rationals is [F1], used in step 1.1 for injectivity of a -> a/1 and in step 2.1 to write every rational as a/b. In step 1.1, thm-int-comm-ring supplies the commutative-ring clause, lem-int-cancellation supplies the absence of zero divisors, lem-nat-embeds-int together with def-natural-numbers supplies 1 != 0 in the integers, and def-zero-divisor-and-integral-domain packages those clauses as the domain hypothesis required by thm-universal-property-of-the-field-of-fractions. All six additions are published and occur earlier in reading order than this order-53.4 example page.

At step 5, prop-localisation-zero-equality-and-kernel-criteria became [F5] and is used in step 1.1 to prove that the universal-property map from Z_6 into Q is injective after its image fraction is zero. cor-prime-iff-euclid-property became [F3] and is used repeatedly in step 3.1 to deduce from q dividing 6^n that the positive prime q divides 2 or 3. The zero criterion is an earlier item on the same order-53.2 A page, and the Euclid-property corollary is published on order 28, so both precede this order-53.4 example.

At step 5, def-localisation-at-a-prime-ideal became [F7] and identifies the denominators in step 1.1 as the integers outside (p). lem-field-is-a-commutative-ring is part of [F1]: it turns the known field Z/pZ into a domain, allowing thm-quotient-is-domain-iff-ideal-prime to prove that (p) is prime. thm-universal-property-of-localisation is [F5] and constructs the map into Q in step 1.1, while prop-localisation-zero-equality-and-kernel-criteria is [F6] and proves that map injective. The definition, universal property, and zero criterion are earlier items on the order-53.2 A page; the field lemma is published on order 46. All precede this order-53.4 example.

At step 5, cor-factor-theorem-over-a-commutative-ring became [F2], used in step 1.1 to identify ker(ev_0)=(x) and in step 1.2 to characterize the allowed denominators by g(0) != 0. cor-maximal-ideals-are-prime is [F6], used in step 1.1 after the quotient-field argument to make (x) prime. def-localisation-at-a-prime-ideal is [F9] and fixes the denominator set in step 1.2; thm-universal-property-of-localisation is [F7] and constructs the map into F(x); prop-localisation-zero-equality-and-kernel-criteria is [F8] and proves it injective. The first two additions are published on orders 52 and 48, and the other three are earlier items on the order-53.2 A page, so all precede this order-53.4 example.

At step 5 the counterexample took a shorter route than planned. Step 1.1 directly enumerates the regular elements of Z/6 as S={1,5}=R^x, and step 2.1 uses the uniqueness clause of thm-universal-property-of-localisation to identify S^{-1}R with R. No step tests when a localization fraction is zero or computes the localization kernel, so prop-localisation-zero-equality-and-kernel-criteria was removed as unused.

At step 5, lem-field-is-a-commutative-ring was added to [F3] because step 2.1 applies thm-polynomial-degree-of-a-product-over-a-domain in K[x] to obtain deg(g)=n-1; the degree theorem requires K to be an integral domain, and K is known there to be a field. The added lemma supplies exactly that field-to-domain bridge. It is published on order 46, earlier than this order-56 page.

At step 5, thm-polynomial-ring-over-a-field-is-a-ufd became [F3]. Step 2.1 uses unique factorisation in E[x] to conclude that every divisor f_j of the split product h has only linear irreducible factors and therefore splits over E. This states the published UFD theorem faithfully and derives the needed divisor-of-a-split-polynomial consequence in the proof. The UFD theorem is published on order 52, earlier than this order-56 page.

At step 5 the induction changed from the generic one-root lemma to a compatible-root construction across the base isomorphism. thm-evaluation-kernel-and-minimal-polynomial is [F2] and makes the chosen root's minimal polynomial divide f in step 1.2; thm-polynomial-ring-over-a-field-is-a-ufd is [F5] and makes its transported divisor split inside E', providing a corresponding root beta in the same step; cor-factor-theorem-over-a-commutative-ring is part of [F6] and supplies f=(x-alpha)g in step 2.1. lem-adjoining-one-root-reduces-the-unsplit-degree was removed because it chooses an unspecified root extension and does not align alpha with beta under sigma; the actual proof instead uses the planned simple-root-adjunction lemma after choosing the compatible roots. All three additions are published on orders 52 or 54, earlier than this order-56 page.

At step 5 the proof built the root-adjunction chain itself because thm-splitting-fields-exist-for-nonzero-polynomials asserts existence but does not expose the chain or the coordinate spanning family, so that planned dependency was removed. lem-adjoining-one-root-reduces-the-unsplit-degree is [F2] and constructs K=F(alpha) with a degree-(n-1) remainder in step 1.2; thm-strong-induction is [F1] and licenses the induction hypothesis and the conclusion in step 4.1; def-factorial-and-falling-factorial is [F5], used for 0!=1 in step 1.1 and n!=n(n-1)! in step 3.1; def-polynomials-that-split-and-splitting-fields is [F6], used to identify the base case and the fields generated by the successive roots in steps 1.1-3.1. The two in-batch additions are earlier items on this order-56 page, and the other two are published earlier in reading order.

At step 5 the planned def-integer-power route was rejected because that definition is for real-number integer powers and has the wrong domain for an arbitrary field extension. def-group-power and lem-group-power-laws instead form [F2], used in step 1.2 to compute (zeta alpha)^n and in step 2.1 to compute (beta alpha^{-1})^n inside the commutative multiplicative group of nonzero field elements. Both replacements are published on order 24, earlier than this order-56 page.

At step 5 the proof made the word permutes explicit rather than stopping at root transport. thm-root-bound-for-polynomials-over-a-domain is [F3] and makes the distinct-root set finite in step 2.1; thm-subset-of-a-finite-set is [F4] and turns the injective self-map of that finite root set into a bijection in the same step. The two additions are published on orders 52 and 20, earlier than this order-56 page.

At step 5, thm-evaluation-kernel-and-minimal-polynomial became [F6]. After Eisenstein proves x^2-2 irreducible, step 1.2 uses [F6] to identify that monic polynomial as the minimal polynomial of sqrt(2), which is the hypothesis needed before the planned simple-extension power-basis theorem yields the basis 1,sqrt(2). The added theorem is published on order 54, earlier than this order-57 example page.

At step 5, cor-splitting-fields-are-unique-up-to-base-isomorphism became [F6]. The factorial theorem only supplies some splitting field with a bounded root-monomial spanning family; step 3.1 uses [F6] to transport that family through a base-fixing isomorphism to the concrete field Q(alpha,omega) identified in step 2.1. The added corollary is an earlier item on the order-56 A page, so it precedes this order-57 example.

At step 5, def-polynomials-that-split-and-splitting-fields became [F4]. Step 1.1 uses its generated-by-the-roots clause to identify Q(sqrt(2)) and Q(sqrt(3)) as the individual splitting fields before step 2.1 applies the planned composite and finite-family results. The added definition is an earlier item on the order-56 A page, so it precedes this order-57 example.

At step 5, thm-polynomial-ring-over-a-field-is-a-ufd became [F6]. In step 2.1 the repeated-root definition shows divisibility by the squares of the two linear factors, but the Statement also says that each factor has exponent exactly two; unique factorisation in [F6] licenses that exact multiplicity conclusion from the displayed factorisation. The UFD theorem is published on order 52, earlier than this order-57 example page.

At step 5 the refutation changed from citing how existing endomorphisms act to explicitly constructing a second automorphism. thm-eisenstein-irreducibility-criterion is [F4] and proves x^2-2 irreducible in step 1.2; lem-an-isomorphism-extends-across-a-simple-root-adjunction is [F3] and then extends the identity on Q while sending sqrt(2) to -sqrt(2), producing the nonidentity automorphism. prop-endomorphisms-of-a-splitting-field-permute-its-roots was removed because it constrains an already-given endomorphism but does not establish that the required nontrivial one exists. The adjunction lemma is an earlier item on the order-56 A page, and Eisenstein is published on order 52; both precede this order-57 false-statement example.
